summary: George Le Grand Jacob worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Elizabeth College and under John Borthwick Gilchrist around 1820–1821, later serving as a teacher at Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1833 to 1835.

George Melville Bolling was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Loyola University Maryland and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield. He held posts at Catholic University of America (1893–1913) and Ohio State University (1914–1940), and was president of the Linguistic Society of America (1931).

George Morrison Carstairs studied at the University of Edinburgh (B.M. circa 1936–1941, Dr.Med. by 1959). He served as Professor of Psychological Medicine at Edinburgh from 1961 to 1973 and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of York from 1973 to 1978.

George Payn Quackenbos, active in Indology and linguistics, completed his A.B. (~1898–1902) and Ph.D. (~1902–1915) at Columbia University. In 1910, he served as an Instructor in Latin at the City College of New York.

George Perrigo Conger worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Cornell, Union Theological Seminary, Berlin, Jena, Heidelberg, the Sorbonne, and Columbia (Ph.D.). He served at the University of Minnesota (1920–1952) and held visiting professorships at Ohio Wesleyan and the University of Calcutta.

George Quasha, active in religious studies and Tibetology, founded Station Hill Press. He held teaching posts at Stony Brook University (~1968–1971) and Bard College (~1974–2005), as well as at The New School and Naropa University.
George R. Elder worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 1978, he studied at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Alex Wayman.
George Read Edward Beresford worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Manager at Cawnpore Bank from around 1845 to 1849 and as manager at Delhi Bank in 1849.

George Rupp is a religious studies scholar who studied at Princeton, Yale, Yale Divinity School, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard. He held posts at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002), and he taught Gary D. DeAngelis.

George Rusby Kaye worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at College of St Mark and St John. He held posts at various schools, the Government Training College, the Bureau of Education, India (until 1923), and the India Office (~1923–1929).
George Saintsbury studied at King's College School (~1858–1863) and Merton College (~1863–1868). He held a post at the University of Edinburgh (~1895–1915) and taught Paul Demiéville.

George Santayana was a philosopher who studied at Boston Latin School, Harvard (Ph.D. under William James), Berlin, and King's College, Cambridge. He taught T. S. Eliot and Beatrice Erskine Lane, and was a philosophy faculty member at Harvard from 1907 to 1912.

George Scott Robertson, working in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Westminster Hospital. He held posts with the Indian Medical Service in 1878 and the Foreign and Political Department in 1888.

George Sherman Lane worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Iowa, Iceland, Paris, and Chicago. After positions at Chicago and Catholic University, he served at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1937–1972) and was a visiting professor at Oslo (1956–1957).

George Shirt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington, and the University of Cambridge. In 1866, he served as a missionary for the Church Mission Society, and he was also a Fellow of the University of Mumbai.

George Smith worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned an LL.D. at the University of Edinburgh by 1868. He served as Professor at Doveton College in 1854 and was a Fellow at the University of Calcutta from 1856 to 1875.

George Speirs Alexander Ranking worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at Aldenham School and St Catharine's College, Cambridge, later serving as Lecturer in Persian at Balliol College, Oxford (1905–1920) and Professor of Persian at the University of Calcutta (1920–1922).

George Thibaut was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Weber, Holtzmann, and Max Müller, receiving his Ph.D. from Berlin. He held leadership posts at Government Sanskrit College, Muir Central College, Queen's College, and served as Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (1907–1914).
George Turnbull Marshall was an Indology scholar who served as Secretary at Fort William College from 1838 to 1852. He also served as Secretary at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1839 to 1840.

George Turnour was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service, working as a Civil Servant in 1818 and becoming Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.
